description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Heartburn / reflux history structure
points: Heartburn is a symptom (rising retrosternal burning). GERD is a diagnosis you may reach later — not the complaint code.
Ask about regurgitation, dysphagia, odynophagia, vomiting, bleeding, weight loss (Bates alarm features).
Exertional 'indigestion' still needs a cardiac screen.

modules.title: Reflux alarm features
points: New dysphagia, odynophagia, weight loss, or GI bleeding with reflux symptoms are alarm features that warrant endoscopy rather than empirical therapy alone.

Q000059.why_ask: Postprandial and lying-flat timing is the classic reflux pattern.
Q000059.think: Typical timing supports reflux but does not itself exclude alarm features.

Q000061.why_ask: A clear symptomatic response to antacids/PPIs supports an acid-related mechanism.
Q000061.think: Poor or no response should prompt reconsideration of the diagnosis rather than simply escalating dose.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: alarm — dysphagia with reflux
points: New dysphagia alongside reflux symptoms is an alarm feature.
This should prompt endoscopy rather than continued empirical treatment.
